newsitem.title: USA: Okla. City Nov home sales up 2.0 pct vs. Nov 1995.
newsitem.headline: Okla. City Nov home sales up 2.0 pct vs. Nov 1995.

text.p: The Oklahoma City Metro Association of REALTORS Inc this week said area home sales posted a modest 2.0 percent gain in November 1996 versus November 1995.

The association said 790 home sales closed in November 1996, accounting for the 2.0 percent gain. The closings brought total volume for November to $67,928,000 up 5.8 percent from the November 1995 total of $64,181,000.
However, November 1996 figures represent a drop from October 1996, when 879 sales closed for a total volume of $75,451,000.
November's average price per home was $85,985. That was up 3.7 percent from the same month in 1995, but up only slightly over the October 1996 average per home price of $85,837.

"This is looking to be (a) slightly better than average season in the Oklahoma City housing market," Peggy Pitts, the association's president said in a release. "With the new year approaching we can take a look back and see that 1996 was an exceptional year for home buyers and sellers in Oklahoma. If all our indicators are correct, 1997 may be a phenomenal year."
